filter.description: A filter tree. A group is exactly one of {"and":[…]}, {"or":[…]}, {"not":{…}} (nest up to 6 levels, 50 conditions). A condition is {"field","op","value"}. Fields: id, username, first_name, last_name, external_id, locale, email, phone, created_at, updated_at, last_sign_in_at, password_updated_at, banned_at, banned, email_verified, mfa_enrolled, mfa_strategy (totp|sms|backup_codes), sign_in_strategy, last_country, last_ip, anonymous, has_password, organization_id, org_role (role key), traits.<key>, public_metadata.<path>, unsafe_metadata.<path>, private_metadata.<path>. Operators: eq, ne, in, nin, contains, starts_with, gt, gte, lt, lte, between ([from,to]), exists (value false = absent). Dates take Unix milliseconds or ISO-8601. Which operators a field takes follows its type; an unsupported one is a 400.

value.description: The value to compare with: a string, number or boolean; a list for in / nin; [from, to] for between; false with exists for "absent".

query.description: Free text over id, names, username, emails and phones, ANDed with the filter.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows the cursor.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to pass as `starting_after` for the next page on a keyset-paginated list; null on the last page (and absent on lists that are not cursor-paginated).

post.summary: Resolve a batch of email addresses to user ids in one call. VERIFIED, LIVE users match by default. For RIGHTS FULFILMENT / DSAR, pass include_unverified:true so an account whose email was never confirmed is still found — otherwise a rights request for such a subject would wrongly complete as "no record". Deleted users are excluded by default (after DELETE /v1/users/:id an address stops resolving here, so a rights orchestrator is not told an erased subject still exists and a uniqueness check does not turn a returning user away); pass include_deleted:true to match them, flagged with `deleted`. (For a DSAR you can skip this lookup entirely by opening the request with subject_email on POST /v1/data_subject_requests, which resolves verified-then-unverified server-side.) Boolean flags also accept "true"/"1"/"yes"/1.

post.summary: Rotate the endpoint signing secret. The new secret is revealed exactly once. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the old secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) every delivery carries two signatures in `atlas-signature` (`v1,<new> v1,<old>`, the new one first), so a verifier holding either secret passes while you deploy the new one; after that only the new secret signs. Set an overlap only once every receiver verifies with an SDK that accepts several signatures (@atlasauth/backend 0.9.1+, Python/Ruby/PHP/Go 0.7.0+, Java 1.5.0+, .NET 1.6.0+, Rust 0.13.0+, Elixir 0.4.0+) or a verifier that splits the header on spaces: a verifier that splits it on ',' rejects every delivery for the whole overlap, even with the new secret. `previous_secret_expires_at` says when the old secret stops signing (epoch ms), or null when it already has; endpoint reads show it too while the overlap is open.

post.summary: Register a Sign in with Atlas app (an OpenID Connect client on https://atlasauth.net) for this platform's account. Body: name, redirect_uris (exact-match https URLs; http://localhost allowed), type (`confidential`, the default, gets a client_secret returned exactly once; `public` uses PKCE and has no secret), optional allowed_scopes (openid, profile, email, offline_access; openid is always required; refresh tokens only with offline_access), logo_url and homepage_url, optional branding (theme, accent_color, background_color, privacy_policy_url, terms_of_service_url) for the sign-in page, post_logout_redirect_uris (exact-match sign-out return URLs for /oauth2/logout, same URL rule as redirect_uris; default []), and backchannel_logout_uri / frontchannel_logout_uri (+ *_session_required) for OIDC back- and front-channel logout. At most 25 apps per account. Honours Idempotency-Key. Keys restricted to specific apps get 403. Idempotent create: `external_ref` returns the existing object on a repeat (200, `idempotent_replay: true`, no secret re-shown); `metadata` tags it (filter lists with ?metadata[key]=value).

parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). post.summary: Rotate the app's webhook signing secret. The new `webhook_secret` is returned once and signs every delivery from now on. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the previous secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) it signs each delivery too, as a second `v1,` entry in `atlas-signature` after the new one, so a verifier holding either secret passes. Set an overlap only once every receiver verifies with an SDK that accepts several signatures (@atlasauth/backend 0.9.1+, Python/Ruby/PHP/Go 0.7.0+, Java 1.5.0+, .NET 1.6.0+, Rust 0.13.0+, Elixir 0.4.0+) or a verifier that splits the header on spaces: a verifier that splits it on ',' rejects every delivery for the whole overlap, even with the new secret. `webhook_previous_secret_expires_at` says when it stops (epoch ms), or null. 409 when the app has no webhook.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the previous secret keeps signing deliveries (as a second atlas-signature entry), in seconds. Default 0: the old secret stops signing at once. At most 604800 (7 days). Set an overlap only once every receiver verifies with an SDK that accepts several signatures (@atlasauth/backend 0.9.1+, Python/Ruby/PHP/Go 0.7.0+, Java 1.5.0+, .NET 1.6.0+, Rust 0.13.0+, Elixir 0.4.0+) or a verifier that splits the header on spaces: a verifier that splits it on ',' rejects every delivery for the whole overlap, even with the new secret.

put.summary: Hand an existing app's grant management to an instance of the same account (adoption), or take it back with `instance_id: null`. That instance's secret key, scoped to `atlas_id_grants:read|write` or `privacy:grants:revoke`, can then list the app (GET /v1/atlas_id_apps), look a person up (…/users?email=) and revoke their grant (DELETE …/grants/{grantId}), here or at /v1/platform/atlas_id_apps/{id}/…, and an erasure on that instance revokes the person's grant (matched by verified email). The app stays yours to edit; `managed_via` becomes `adopted`. 404 for an instance of another account; 409 for the app of an instance's Sign in with Atlas toggle (already managed). delete.summary: Revoke one user's grant to this app (grant_id from the users lookup): the approval is forgotten, so the next sign-in shows the consent screen again; the app's refresh tokens for the user stop working; a back-channel logout goes to the app (and its logout fan-out endpoints) for each live sign-in, and the app's webhook gets grant.revoked. The person's Atlas account and other apps are untouched. Also accepts an instance secret key (`secretKey`) with `atlas_id_grants:write` (or the `privacy:grants:revoke` / `privacy:execute` presets), for the apps that instance manages or has adopted (PUT …/managed_by); any other app is 404 to it.

post.summary: Move one Sign in with Atlas app from one origin to another: rewrites every field that points at `from` (scheme + host + port) to `to`, keeping each URL's path: redirect_uris, post_logout_redirect_uris, backchannel_logout_uri, frontchannel_logout_uri, homepage_url, logo_url, jwks_uri and the branding privacy_policy_url / terms_of_service_url. Returns the before → after diff and the app. dry_run: true writes nothing; a value the field would refuse makes a real run a 422 without writing; a second run returns an empty diff. Logged on GET /v1/platform/config_changelog. Apps managed by an instance toggle are 409.

patch.summary: Update allowed origins and auth_config (a partial, validated, merged patch — not a replace). Open or public-suffix wildcard origins refused (a single-label https://*.your-domain.com is accepted; shared hosts like *.vercel.app on development instances only); an invalid auth_config returns 422. A method that needs email (email code, email link, password sign-up that verifies by email) is accepted even when the instance has no email provider yet (email is bring-your-own; Terraform or config import may add the provider later in the same apply): the response lists it under inactive_methods, users are not offered it, and it becomes active on its own once a provider is configured (PUT /v1/messaging_providers/email). Captcha always runs on your own provider keys: turning a captcha ON for a flow (or changing its provider) before both the provider site key (auth_config.captcha.siteKey) and its secret (PUT /v1/instance/captcha_secret) are set returns 422 CAPTCHA_KEYS_REQUIRED with param naming the missing one — store the secret first, then enable. Removing the site key while a flow uses it returns 409 CAPTCHA_IN_USE unless force=true, which also turns the captcha off on those flows. Setting the retired raw branding fields (branding.customCss / customHtmlHeader / customHtmlFooter) returns 422 naming the field — use the design settings (PUT /v1/instance/design) instead; clearing them (null or "") is accepted. The response echoes auth_config_resolved so you can confirm the change took effect, and `warnings`: an origin_still_referenced entry for every removed origin that webhook endpoints (not marked external) or OAuth client URIs still point at, naming each one and the POST /v1/instance/move_origin call that moves them. Strict writes: auth_config.strictRequestBodies (true on instances created from 2026-10 on) refuses unknown body fields with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD on every Backend API write; set it to opt in or out, or send Atlas-Strict: true | false on one request.

put.summary: Bring your own key: keep the signing key in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault. Atlas validates the settings, reads (or creates) a key version, proves it can sign with it, saves the settings (credentials encrypted under the instance key) and rotates the main signing key to it — the previous key stays published for `grace_period_seconds` unless `emergency`. A KMS that refuses (bad credentials, missing permission, wrong key type) is a 422 naming the reason. SAML assertions, AuthnRequests and metadata certificates are signed by the KMS key too (an RS256 key when one is configured). Audited as signing_key.provider_configured.

Optional `secondary`: a second key for the other algorithm, so APIs on it sign with a key of their own — aws_kms `{ alg, key_id? }`, gcp_kms `{ crypto_key, key_version? }` (a CryptoKey of the other algorithm), azure_key_vault `{ key_name, key_version?, alg }`. Each key must be of its algorithm's type.

Never extends past the session's absolute expiry and never revives an ended session — a revoked session is 409 SESSION_REVOKED, a session that already timed out is 409 SESSION_IDLE_EXPIRED, and one past its absolute expiry is 409 SESSION_EXPIRED; an unknown id is 404. At most one effective write per minute per session: a touch within 60 seconds of the session's last activity returns the current state with extended:false, so calling it on every request is safe. No request body. Returns the session with last_active_at and idle_expires_at.

post.summary: Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once), OR import an existing key by its SHA-256 hash (hash_algorithm "sha256" or "sha256_hex") so it verifies against the original secret. Normally authenticated with an sk_ key; a LAN/offline MACHINE may instead self-provision a key for ITSELF by presenting Authorization: Bearer <machine JWT> (token_use:m2m from /v1/machines/token) + x-publishable-key — the subject is forced to that machine and it cannot grant itself management-plane scopes. Pass public_key (an SPKI PEM) to make the key proof-of-possession: tokens minted from it carry cnf.jkt and a resource verifies a holder-signed proof OFFLINE. Pass limits (an array of { unit, amount, period } with period request|day|month|total) to set per-key spend caps, metered with POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/usage. post.summary: Managed email: Atlas sets up your sending domain (the domain of `from_address`) on YOUR OWN Resend or Brevo account, with your API key, and sends through it once the domain is verified. Pass `transport` ("resend" | "brevo") with `config.api_key`, or `provider_id` of your configured Resend or Brevo email provider; without either the call is refused with 422 (param `config.api_key`). The key is stored, write-only, as the instance's email provider in `managed_domain` mode. Returns 201 with the DNS `records` to publish (DKIM, SPF / return-path for Resend; ownership, DKIM, DMARC for Brevo). Until the domain is verified email delivery stays unavailable and preflight warns `managed_email_unverified`. Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the records itself (DNS-only; the token is write-only) and verifies in the same call when DNS propagates in time. Atlas also registers a bounce / complaint webhook on your Resend or Brevo account, for this instance only (`feedback_webhook`); the counts appear in `usage`. No Atlas sending limits apply (`limits: null`): the account and its limits are yours. Atlas never uses an email account of its own. 409 when the domain is set up on another Atlas instance; 502 MANAGED_EMAIL_PROVIDER_ERROR when your provider refuses.

Without a valid secret both headers are ignored. On rotation the replaced secret keeps working for `overlap_seconds` (default 86400, 0 = stop now, at most 604800).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

overlap_seconds.description: On rotation: how long the replaced secret keeps working. Default 86400; 0 = stop now.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

saml_idp_slo_binding.description: How logout messages are sent to the IdP: `redirect` (default) or `post`; null resets to redirect.

saml_idp_slo_soap_url.description: The IdP SOAP-binding SingleLogoutService (https). When set, a session ended server-side (admin or API revoke, ban, deletion, password reset) is logged out at the IdP over this back channel.

parameters.description: Page size, 1-500. Without limit (and without starting_after) the whole list is returned.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor: return only items after this one. Pass the previous page's `next_cursor` (the last item's id). An unknown cursor is a 400.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to pass as `starting_after` for the next page on a keyset-paginated list; null on the last page (and absent on lists that are not cursor-paginated).

post.summary: Create a self-service SSO onboarding profile: allowed connection types and an optional bound organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

422.description: Unprocessable. Includes UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends `Atlas-Strict: true` (or the instance enables strict request bodies) and the body has a field this endpoint does not accept.

The hosted pages offer only these when the sign-in is for this app; a session made another way signs in again at /oauth2/authorize.

branding.description: The heading, sub-heading, logo and primary colour of the hosted sign-in and sign-up pages when the sign-in is for this app.

writable_traits.description: The identity traits a session that came from this app (a native app that exchanged its token for a session) may change through PATCH /v1/client/me. Others are refused with 403.

enabled.description: Turn risk-based MFA on or off for sign-ins to this app.

mode.description: audit scores and records sign-ins without changing them.

mid_session.description: The refresh-time check for sessions that came from this app (its native token exchange).

risk.description: Overrides of the instance's riskBasedMfa for sign-ins to this app (a sign-in started from this app's /oauth2/authorize request). A field left null keeps the instance value; weights, signals and reputation feeds stay instance-wide.

post.summary: Trust an external issuer for this client. With purpose user_assertion (default) its signed JWTs (verified against the inline jwks or the https jwks_uri) can then be presented to POST /oauth2/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer. subject_mapping says how the JWT sub names an Atlas user. With purpose client_auth or both (PRO-06 workload identity) a client registered with token_endpoint_auth_method workload_jwt authenticates by presenting a token from this issuer as its client_assertion; subject_pattern is then required and must name the workload. workload_kind github_actions, gcp and azure fill in the issuer and JWKS URL. post.summary: Claim a custom domain (fapi or accounts). Returns 201 with the full custom_domain object — including its `id` (dom_…), which you pass to POST /v1/domains/{id}/verify once DNS is published — plus the CNAME `instructions` to follow (or a `note` for a platform subdomain, which is live immediately). Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the CNAME itself: it finds the zone, creates the record DNS-only (never proxied; `dns.proxied: true` is refused), waits briefly for it to resolve and verifies, so the domain can go from nothing to active in one call (`verified` in the response; otherwise call verify later). The token is stored encrypted and is never readable back (the response shows only `dns.provider` and `token_set`). An existing record that points elsewhere is not overwritten unless `dns.overwrite` is true (409 DNS_RECORD_CONFLICT); a rejected token is 422 DNS_TOKEN_REJECTED; no visible zone is 422 DNS_ZONE_NOT_FOUND.

get.summary: Check your setup in one call. Lists findings about configuration the server can see is broken or worth knowing — no sign-in method enabled, a social provider enabled without credentials, OAuth clients without redirect or post-logout URIs, a first-party client origin missing from allowed_origins, an allowed https origin that login readiness would fail (CORS or session cookie), sign-up that new users cannot complete, custom domains not serving yet, email or SMS sign-in without a provider, a Cookie Munch site that does not match the sign-in host, an OAuth client whose back-channel logout URI is failing (oauth_client_backchannel_failing: 3 consecutive failed deliveries, or one answered with a redirect, which Atlas never follows), a webhook endpoint whose last delivery was redirected (webhook_endpoint_redirecting), a webhook endpoint that is failing (webhook_endpoint_failing: a failure streak is running), switched off after repeated failures (webhook_endpoint_disabled: an error when it carries session or account events) or on a host that is not one of the instance origins or redirect hosts (webhook_endpoint_off_origin, unless it is marked external), a first-party client without a back-channel logout URI (oauth_client_no_backchannel_logout_uri), and the security posture group (group: security_posture — pkce_not_required, passkey_without_uv, auto_link_unverified) — each with a severity, a stable code, a plain message and the fix. A finding that does not apply to how the instance integrates (the embedded-component checks on an origin Atlas is confident signs in through the hosted redirect) is listed under suppressed with the reason, not in findings; integrations shows how each allowed origin was judged. ok is true when there are no errors. ok covers configuration; to confirm a browser can sign in on a given origin, use GET /v1/diagnostics/login_readiness?origin=… for each production origin. Every code is listed by GET /v1/instance/preflight/codes. Read-only.

parameters.name: min_severity
parameters.description: Only findings at least this severe (warning = warnings and errors). Default info (everything). ok still covers every finding.

parameters.name: include_suppressed
parameters.description: true = also list the suppressed findings in findings, marked suppressed: true with suppressed_reason.

sdk_versions_seen.description: Atlas browser SDK versions that called this instance in the last 7 days (newest first), each with the advisories that apply to it.

reason.description: Stable code, e.g. email_code_sign_in (the reason= of the Atlas-SDK-Advisory header).

ok.description: True when there are no error-severity findings. It covers configuration: whether a browser can actually sign in on an origin is what GET /v1/diagnostics/login_readiness answers (preflight reports every allowed https origin that would fail it).

min_severity.description: The lowest severity listed in findings (the ?min_severity filter; info = everything).

findings.description: Ordered error, then warning, then info. Only findings at or above min_severity.

suppressed.description: Findings that do not apply to how this instance integrates (for example the embedded-component cookie check on an origin that signs in through the hosted redirect), with the reason. Not counted in ok.

integrations.description: How each allowed https origin signs in, as preflight judged it: declared in allowed_origins, inferred from embedded SDK traffic or from its OAuth clients, or the embedded default.

confident.description: False only for the default (nothing says how the origin signs in).

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of the instance's new events for a listen session. Each `webhook` event carries `{id, type, headers, body}`: the headers (`atlas-id`, `atlas-timestamp`, `atlas-signature`) and the exact JSON body of a would-be delivery, signed with the session secret. Starts at "now" unless resumed with `Last-Event-ID` or `after`. Query: `events` (comma-separated types or patterns), `max_events` and `max_wait_seconds` (end the stream early, for scripts and CI). A `: keep-alive` comment is sent every 15 seconds; an `expired` event ends the stream at the session expiry. 404 for an unknown session id, 400 once expired.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Comma-separated event types or patterns (`user.*`).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this event id.

parameters.name: max_events
parameters.description: Close the stream after this many forwarded events.

parameters.name: poll_ms
parameters.description: How often the stream checks for new events, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: max_wait_seconds
parameters.description: Close the stream after this long.

200.description: Server-Sent Events: `ready`, then one `webhook` event per forwarded event (data: {id, type, headers, body}), `: keep-alive` comments, and `expired` at the end of the session.

post.summary: Start a one-click connection to a referral platform (`:preset` is `referalli` or any platform listed in `one_click_presets` of the settings): returns the platform's authorize URL (OAuth, PKCE). The merchant picks an organization and program there; the platform creates the connection and returns its signing secret to Atlas server to server, so nothing is copied. For Referalli, Atlas then requires v2 signatures and registers the two-way sync webhook; it pings either way. Referrals stay off until you turn them on. 404 for an unknown preset; 422 REFERRALS_NOT_CONFIGURED when this deployment does not offer it (see `available` in `one_click_presets`): connect with a key or the signing secret instead. Any platform can implement the install: see the referral protocol guide.

post.summary: Create a custom OAuth 2.0 / OIDC provider (Atlas is the relying party). OIDC: give the issuer and the endpoints are discovered (a bad issuer is a 400 now, not a broken button later). Set client authentication (client_secret_basic/post/jwt, private_key_jwt with an Atlas-held key, or none), a declarative profile_mapping, upstream logout and third-party initiated login. The response names the URLs to register at the provider. Starts disabled unless `enabled: true` (which needs a client id, a secret for the secret methods, and a signing key for private_key_jwt).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

post.summary: Define a connection: an owner (an organization or a user) and a third-party API. `kind` is oauth (rides a linked provider account; for an organization, the account of the member who shared it), api_key or client_credentials (a credential the owner enters). `allowed_hosts` lists the only hosts the relay may call. An owner may hold several connections of one provider (one per provider account): create one per account, then call `POST /v1/connections/{id}/connect`. A connection is never a sign-in method.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

provider.description: A built-in or custom OAuth provider key for oauth; any short key otherwise.

allowed_methods.description: Relay verbs allowed for this connection (default GET, HEAD, POST).

environment.description: The provider environment the credential belongs to. sandbox selects the provider's test hosts (Salesforce test.salesforce.com, PayPal and QuickBooks sandboxes, DocuSign demo...).

Each key is checked against that provider's allowlist pattern; a value that is not a plain label or public hostname is refused with 400 `host_params.<key>`.

purpose.description: Only data is accepted. A sign-in link is an external account.

kind.description: oauth, github_app_installation, admin_consent and a three-legged oauth1 are authorized by a browser step; client_credentials and jwt_bearer mint tokens from a credential Atlas holds; api_key, bearer, basic, custom_header and hmac_secret are typed secrets the owner enters.

name.description: Your label for this account, for example "Support inbox".

allowed_hosts.description: The only hosts the relay may call with this connection.

config.description: Non-secret settings of the kind (api_key placement and name, token_url, client_id, scopes, issuer, audience, public_jwk, signature_method, realm, installation_id, tenant...). Never a secret.

status.description: needs_reauth: the token expired or was refused and cannot be refreshed. revoked: disconnected on purpose.

purpose.description: A connection is never a sign-in method: connecting one adds no way to sign in, counts toward no only-method rule and needs no step-up.

environment.description: The provider environment the credential belongs to. sandbox selects the provider's test hosts (Salesforce test.salesforce.com, PayPal and QuickBooks sandboxes, DocuSign demo...).

host_params.description: Values that fill the provider's host templates for this one connection, for example {"subdomain":"acme"} (Zendesk), {"shop":"acme"} (Shopify), {"domain":"acme.my.salesforce.com"} (Salesforce My Domain), {"data_center":"eu"} (Zoho), {"tenant":"contoso.onmicrosoft.com"} (Microsoft), {"host":"git.example.com"} (self-managed GitLab). Each key is checked against that provider's allowlist pattern; a value that is not a plain label or public hostname is refused with 400 `host_params.<key>`.

post.summary: Start the provider authorization for this connection and return the URL to send the owner to. The tokens are stored on the connection itself, never on a user: no external account is created, no sign-in method is added, no email is proven and no step-up is needed. `host_params` fill the provider's host templates for this connection (validated against a per-provider allowlist; 400 `host_params.<key>` otherwise). Reconnecting the same provider account updates the same connection; a different account answers 409 unless `create_if_new` is true. An owner OAuth client (`PUT /v1/connections/oauth_clients`) overrides the instance client.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

redirect_url.description: Where the owner lands after the provider returns. Must be an allowed origin of the instance.

host_params.description: Values that fill the provider's host templates for this one connection, for example {"subdomain":"acme"} (Zendesk), {"shop":"acme"} (Shopify), {"domain":"acme.my.salesforce.com"} (Salesforce My Domain), {"data_center":"eu"} (Zoho), {"tenant":"contoso.onmicrosoft.com"} (Microsoft), {"host":"git.example.com"} (self-managed GitLab). Each key is checked against that provider's allowlist pattern; a value that is not a plain label or public hostname is refused with 400 `host_params.<key>`.

environment.description: The provider environment the credential belongs to. sandbox selects the provider's test hosts (Salesforce test.salesforce.com, PayPal and QuickBooks sandboxes, DocuSign demo...).

additional_scopes.description: Scopes to ask for on top of the provider defaults, the owner client's scopes and config.scopes.

display.description: popup completes through postMessage like a popup sign-in.

create_if_new.description: When the provider returns a different account than the one this connection already holds, create a sibling connection for it instead of answering 409.

connect_user_id.description: Informational: the user who is connecting (stored as authorized_by_user_id).

authorization_url.description: Send the owner here. The provider returns to Atlas, the tokens are stored on the connection, and the owner lands on your redirect_url with `__atlas_status=connected` and `__atlas_connection=<id of the connection that was written>`.

422.description: Unprocessable. Includes UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends `Atlas-Strict: true` (or the instance enables strict request bodies) and the body has a field this endpoint does not accept.

post.summary: Revoke the stored token at the provider, delete it from the vault and mark the connection revoked (connection.revoked is sent once). The local token is cleared in every case. Connect again to use it.

get.summary: The connection's live token for your backend. An oauth connection's token is refreshed first when it is expired or about to be (single-flight across processes, using the client that issued it and the connection's host_params). Built for sync workers: the response carries an `ETag` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=<seconds until just before expires_at>`, so cache it until then; send `If-None-Match` and an unchanged, still-valid token answers 304 with no body and no vault read; `min_ttl_seconds` refreshes first when less than that much validity remains. A grant connection (client_credentials, jwt_bearer, github_app_installation, admin_consent) has its token minted from the credential Atlas holds instead, answered with `Cache-Control: no-store` (no ETag); pass `subject` to a jwt_bearer connection to act as that user (Google domain-wide delegation). Includes the captured handles (`metadata`, `token_response`) and any further named credentials. 402 CONNECTION_REQUIRED with `meta.reason` not_connected, needs_reauth, revoked or refresh_failed when there is no usable token. When the provider answers 401 to the token, call `POST /v1/connections/{id}/token/refresh` instead of re-reading. Rate limit: 6,000 reads per minute per secret key and 300 per minute per connection (RateLimit-* headers on every response, 429 with Retry-After beyond them). Reads are audited as connection.token_read once per connection per minute with the read count (a read that refreshed is always audited); the token itself is never logged.

post.summary: Rotate the signing secret of the integration's event receiver. The new secret is revealed exactly once. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the old secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) every delivery carries two signatures in `Atlas-Signature` (`v1,<new> v1,<old>`, the new one first), so the service verifies with either secret while it deploys the new one; after that only the new secret signs. `previous_secret_expires_at` says when the old secret stops signing (epoch ms), or null when it already has. Audited as integration.<id>.events_secret_rotated. 404 when the integration has no event receiver.

publish_resource_metadata.description: Atlas serves RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata for this API at /oauth2/resource-metadata?resource=<identifier>.

OrgPolicy.description: Org policy override object. Keys are camelCase (mirrors readOrgPolicy). Only set overrides appear.

passwordPolicyOverride.description: Tighten-only password rules layered over the instance policy: minLength, bannedPasswords, and checkBreaches/requireUppercase/requireLowercase/requireNumber/requireSymbol (true only).

allowedSignInMethods.description: Restrict which sign-in methods a member may use (e.g. "password", "passkey", "oauth", "oauth:google", "saml", "magic_link"). Empty/absent = all methods. Enforced by membership; most-restrictive across the user's orgs.

ipAllowlist.description: CIDR allow-list gating sign-in for members (e.g. "203.0.113.0/24"). Empty/absent = unrestricted. Most-restrictive across the user's orgs.

maxSessionAgeSeconds.description: Cap the absolute session lifetime for members, in seconds (300 … 7776000). Null/absent = instance default. Smallest cap across the user's orgs wins.

memberVisibility.description: What ordinary members see of each other in Frontend API member lists: directory (default: name and picture) or private (member id and role only). Members who manage memberships always see names, plus the primary email and MFA status.

native.description: True when this provider signs in through an in-page native library (e.g. Google One Tap / GSI) that verifies an id_token, rather than a redirect. A native provider also requires its `javascript_origins` to be registered on the provider console.

redirect_uri.description: The exact callback URL to register at the provider console.

atlas_callback.description: Atlas's own callback URL; a custom_redirect_uri forwards ?code&state here.

custom_redirect_uri.description: A tenant's own already-registered callback (migration): Atlas uses it in the authorize + token exchange and it forwards to atlas_callback. Null when unset.

enabled.description: Whether the provider is turned on. Saving credentials via PUT does NOT enable it; toggle with POST /v1/oauth_providers/{provider}/enabled.

icon_url.description: The instance's per-provider icon override, or null.

collect_on.description: When the field is asked for. sign_up (default): the sign-up form. next_sign_in: held at the next sign-in that finds it empty. before_feature: asked by the application via GET /v1/client/me/profile_completion.

reprompt_days.description: An optional next_sign_in field the user skipped is asked again after this many days (default 30; 0 = never).

audiences.description: Per-audience branding for the hosted sign-in and sign-up pages, keyed by audience hint (1-32 characters: a-z, 0-9, _ and -; at most 20). A sign-in started with audience_hint=<hint> (on /oauth2/authorize or the hosted page URL) uses that entry's heading, subheading, logo and primary colour; any other hint gets the default branding. PATCH merges per hint: an entry replaces that hint, null deletes it, audiences: null removes them all.

subheading.description: Replaces the line under the heading.

primaryColor.description: Replaces the primary colour (hex, rgb() or a CSS colour name).

BrandingSettings.description: The editable branding settings (sign-in page, emails, hosted pages). Every field is optional. Retired keys may still appear on read.

primaryColor.description: Replaces the primary colour (hex, rgb() or a CSS colour name).

BrandingPatch.description: A partial branding change. Every field is optional and replaces the stored value; inside socialButtons each per-provider map merges per key, a null value deletes that key, a null map clears it, and socialButtons: null removes the whole bag. audiences merges per audience hint the same way. A field this endpoint does not know is ignored and named in Atlas-Unknown-Fields, or refused with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends Atlas-Strict: true.

resolved.description: What the renderers use, after dropping anything unsafe or invalid. Every writable field appears here under the same name and shape you write it (fontFamily, providers, copy, legal, theme, layout, card, interaction, …), holding the value in force: compare your desired state against this object alone. A field you did not set shows its default. Also carries derived renderer values (escapedName, fontStack, providerOrder, providerHidden, eyebrow, headline, subheadline, footer). The retired raw fields customCss / customHtmlHeader / customHtmlFooter resolve to "" unless set on Atlas's own instance.

audiences.description: Every audience the hosted page can theme for, as it reads them (invalid values dropped).

fontFamily.description: The font stack name in force (system when unset or unknown).

fontStack.description: The CSS font-family list fontFamily resolves to.

reason.description: Reason code returned when the rule matches.

groups.description: The endpoint groups a rule may name.

replaces_built_in.description: The built-in budget a rule on this group replaces; null when a rule is added on top.

key.description: ip: per client IP; user: per signed-in user (Frontend API) or the user in the path (Backend API), falling back to the IP or key; instance: one budget for every caller.

deletion_effective_at.description: Erasures: epoch ms when the account is erased — the date every executor aligns on.

status.description: A deferred erasure is `scheduled` (held in its grace window with a `scheduled_for`/`eta`), distinguishing it from a `pending` request that runs on the next worker pass. The worker promotes it to `processing` once due, then `completed`. `cancelled` = aborted in the grace window; `rejected` = a DPO declined it.

eta.description: Estimated completion (epoch ms). An erasure = the grace-window deadline; an export = null (runs async). Alias of scheduled_for.

result.description: Export requests: the data-export bundle once fulfilled (only on single-request reads); otherwise null.

Omitted on an update: the stored mode is kept for the same transport. managed_domain is set only by managed email.

config.description: Provider settings. Unknown keys are refused. Required when first configuring webhook (or switching to it): url, signing_secret. When updating the same transport, an omitted or empty secret keeps the stored value.

url.description: Your HTTPS delivery endpoint (port 443). Atlas POSTs each message here, Standard Webhooks signed.

signing_secret.description: Secret that signs every delivery (whsec_… base64 or any string). Write-only: never returned.

payload.description: Email only. rendered (default) sends the final subject/text/html; raw sends the template name and variables.
